title: Regional transit fare calculator
original_request: Build a service that tells a rider what a journey will cost before they travel, including transfers and concession eligibility, for the four operators in the region.

objective.statement: Publish a fare calculation service that returns the price of a journey across the region's four transit operators, including transfer rules and concession eligibility, that an operator can verify against their own published tariff.

deliverables.text: A fare quote API taking origin, destination, time and rider class.
A machine readable tariff per operator, versioned by effective date.
A quote explanation showing every rule that contributed to a price.

success_criteria.text: Quotes match each operator's published tariff on an agreed sample of journeys.
Every quote can be explained rule by rule without reading the code.

constraints.text: A fare rule is only valid if it cites the operator document it came from, with an effective date.
Where the tariff is ambiguous the service returns a range and says why, rather than picking a number.
Concession eligibility is never inferred from anything the rider did not state.
A quote must be computable without a network call to an operator.

requirements.text: Transfers within 90 minutes of the first validation are charged as one journey, per the regional agreement.
Peak pricing applies by validation time, not by journey start, when an operator defines it that way.
Every quote carries the ordered list of rule ids that produced it.
Where two operators claim the same zone the cheaper tariff applies.

decisions.text: Tariffs are data, not code, so an operator can review a change without a release.
decisions.rationale: Fare changes arrive as documents on a schedule nobody controls.

decisions.text: The explanation is produced by the same pass that produces the price.
decisions.rationale: An explanation generated separately from the calculation will eventually disagree with it.

decisions.text: Quotes are computed from a local tariff snapshot.
decisions.rationale: Operator endpoints are not available at the latency a quote needs.

acceptance_criteria.text: The agreed sample of 500 journeys matches each operator's published tariff exactly.
Every quote in the sample carries an explanation naming only rules that exist.
Ambiguous journeys return a range, and the ranges are reviewed by the operator.
A tariff change takes effect on its stated date without a deployment.

findings.text: Two operators start the transfer clock at validation and one starts it at boarding, which differ on long platforms.
Concession categories are consistent across operators but the proof each accepts is not.

unknowns.question: Where two operators claim the same zone, whose tariff applies?
unknowns.impact: Affects every cross boundary journey and the whole transfer model.

unknowns.question: Is rounding applied per leg or per journey?
unknowns.impact: Changes totals by small amounts on most multi leg journeys.

tasks.text: Import the four published tariffs as versioned data.
Implement the transfer window, including the boarding versus validation difference.
Agree the 500 journey sample with each operator.

project_state.summary: Tariffs imported and transfer rules in progress. The zone overlap question blocks the cross boundary cases.

history.summary: Open the record from the original request.
Record the four constraints and the tariff source rule.
Accept the transfer window and peak pricing requirements.
